render_job_readback: EncodingProfile and MultiPassEncode are listed by GetRenderJobList; DataBurnIn and ExportSubtitle are not (2026-10-02)
fusion_output_cache: SetFusionOutputCache takes the CacheMode constants (resolve.CACHE_AUTO_ENABLED -1.0, CACHE_ENABLED 1.0, CACHE_DISABLED 0.0) and refuses every string (Auto, On, Off, Enabled, Disabled); GetIsFusionOutputCacheEnabled reads -1 (auto) on a new clip comp and the value set after that (2026-10-02)
edit_page_fade_on_title_range: SetFades on a Text+ range reads back; FadeIn n renders alpha k/n from 0 on the first frame (the preview's comp fade is (k+1)/n), FadeOut 3 renders 1, 0.5, 0 on the last three frames (the preview 0.67, 0.33, 0): not used for titles, the comp fade matches the preview (2026-10-02)
timeline_item_labels: TimelineItem.SetName and SetClipColor change the timeline item only, never its media pool clip; SetClipColor refuses a name outside the 16 clip colours (2026-10-02)
timeline_comments: a timeline's media pool item takes SetClipProperty Comments; GetClipProperty reads the line breaks back as spaces (2026-10-02)
track_enabled_read_needs_current: GetIsTrackEnabled on a timeline that is not current read False for every video track of a copy whose V1 and V2 were enabled; with the copy current it read True, True, False, False, False as set (2026-10-02)
notes: Stills (2026-09-30, sandbox, 21.1.0.14): AppendToTimeline ignores startFrame and endFrame for a still image and always places the Standard Still Duration (125 frames at 25 fps), also with startFrame 1920 (a still's clip start reads 1920). Marks on the media pool item are honoured: SetMarkInOut(0, n - 1), then an append without startFrame and endFrame, gives exactly n frames (measured 44 and 50), and ClearMarkInOut afterwards keeps the placed length. ZoomX, ZoomY, Pan, Tilt and SetFades work on the placed still. The build places stills this way and verify checks them by record range and length only.

Text+ (2026-09-30): Timeline.InsertFusionTitleIntoTimeline ripple-inserts on V1 at the playhead (it split a clip and pushed its tail 125 frames later) and takes no track or length, so it is only ever called on the build's own graphics timeline, never on the programme. Each title and caption gets one Text+ there, one 125 frame slot apart (the default generator length at 25 fps); ranges of that timeline are then appended onto the programme at exact record frames and lengths. Template inputs are set with SetInput and never inside comp.Lock() (values read back but do not render).

Text+ look (2026-09-30, measured on Edit page grabs of a 1080x1920 timeline with Arial Bold): Size = font pixels / (0.70 x timeline width) (a second run gave 0.72); Center is {1: x, 2: 1 - y from the top} because Fusion's y runs up; the default line pitch is the font's own line height, 1.15 em for Arial (two lines at Size 0.075 sat 66 px apart with a 56.7 px em), so LineSpacing = wanted pitch / 1.15; the outline element (element 2) defaults to RED, so its colour is always set, and ElementShape2 is left alone (0 turned it into a fill); Thickness2 0.08 drew about 0.07 em outside the glyph; the box element (element 4, Level 0 = one box around all lines) keeps about 0.30 em of margin at the sides even with ExtendHorizontal4 0, then grows 1.26 em per unit of ExtendHorizontal4 and 1.43 em per unit of ExtendVertical4 above and below the lines. These box factors come from two grabs; pixel verify masks text boxes, and the structure verify reads the text back.

Subtitle tracks (2026-09-30): never call MediaPool.AppendToTimeline with a subtitle media pool item (an imported SRT). One form ignored recordFrame and put every cue 25 s late, and the form with startFrame, endFrame and recordFrame crashed Resolve 21.1.0.14. Captions are built as Text+ cues instead; export-srt stays for platforms that take caption files.

Frame grabs (2026-09-30): Project.ExportCurrentFrameAsStill works on the Edit page in 21.1 without a page switch and writes the full timeline output (Text+, nested timelines and stills included) as a PNG at the timeline size, about 0.46 s per grab; it matched the rendered frame at correlation 0.9998 to 1.0 and told the two sides of a cut apart. It moves the playhead, so the grab snippet restores it.

Fusion and other hazards (2026-09-30): clip Fusion comps run in SOURCE frames (a 50 fps clip over 50 timeline frames renders comp frames 0 to 98); Dynamic Zoom enabled by script cannot be steered and zooms OUT by default; there is no render settings key for audio normalisation (loudness is set by the Deliver page tick or a normalised mix); ExportRenderPreset of a built in preset returns False.
Measured in a separate sandbox project with barcode clips (25, 30, 50 and 100 fps on a 25 fps timeline) and rendered frames; every rendered frame matched the rules below.

Mixed rates at speed 1: n source frames of a clip at media rate M on a timeline at rate T last floor(n * T / M) timeline frames, and never less than 1. Measured with 24, 23.976, 25, 29.97, 30, 50 and 60 fps clips on 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 50 and 60 fps timelines (about 4700 placements, no exception): 13 frames of 30 fps on 25 give 10, 3 frames of 29.97 on 25 give 2, 7 frames of 24 on 30 give 8, 4 frames of 25 on 30 give 4, 10 frames of 30 on 29.97 give 9. Media slower than the timeline therefore skips some lengths (a 24 fps clip on 30 can be 3 or 5 frames but never 4); the lab only makes lengths Resolve can place, and validate names the nearest ones (rate_length).
Nearest retime floors: a 30 fps clip on 25 fps shows 0 1 2 3 4 6 7 8 9 10 12, and 50 % speed shows 0 0 1 1 2 2.
append_end exclusive: startFrame 10, endFrame 20 gives 10 frames. endFrame equal to the clip's frame count is accepted and plays the last frame, so no tail trim is needed.

SetSpeed with RippleTimeline False keeps the item's timeline length and changes the source it plays (20 frames at 50 % play 10 source frames). The build therefore places a retimed item at its final length first, then sets the speed.

Pan and Tilt are in timeline pixels scaled to the image after input sizing: the image moves Pan * (image width after sizing / timeline width). A 16:9 source on a 9:16 crop timeline moves 3.16 pixels per unit of Pan and 1 pixel per unit of Tilt. Zoom scales about the frame centre and does not change the pan distance. Positive Pan moves right, positive Tilt moves up.

GetSourceStartTime and GetSourceEndTime of an item under a transition include the frames the transition borrows (the incoming clip of a centred 12 frame dissolve reads 6 frames early); the picture at the cut is right. verify corrects for it.
A centred transition needs handles on both clips; without the incoming clip's head handle AddTransition returns None. A right-aligned one needs only the outgoing clip's tail.

AppendToTimeline with a trackIndex above the track count silently places the clip on track 1, so the build adds tracks first. An overlapping or locked-track append returns a list holding None and changes nothing.
Clips with rotation metadata (vertical phone or camera clips) are shown rotated: Resolve reports the rotated resolution, like the lab proxies.
Rendering through the API switches Resolve to the Deliver page; creating a timeline and appending clips switches it to the Edit page.

Audio: AudioVolume -8 matched -8.00 dB exactly and the render's audio lined up with the preview to the sample. Resolve's audio fade curve is a little steeper than the preview's linear fade (2 to 4 dB lower in the middle of a 1 s fade).

Audio tracks of a clip: a clip whose media pool audio mapping has several tracks (a 4 channel camera file maps as 4 mono tracks, two stereo streams as 2 stereo tracks) is spread over the following timeline audio tracks by AppendToTimeline; when one of them holds an item (the music on A2) the whole clip is refused, picture included, and on the last track only its first track is placed. With the other audio tracks locked for the append, one item lands on the target track: the clip's first audio track (channel 1 mono, or stream 1 stereo), and the picture links normally. The build does that, and the lab's WAV is the same first track. TimelineItem.SetSourceAudioChannelMapping returns True and reads back the new mapping, but the rendered sound does not change, so channel choice happens in Clip Attributes before the dump.
A mono clip plays at unity on both sides of a stereo track (render -21.07 dB per side for a -21.07 dB source); the lab's WAV does the same.

FCPXML import (File > Import > Timeline, MediaPool.ImportTimelineFromFile): srcEnable is ignored, so an A/V asset used for picture only brings its camera sound at 0 dB and linked sound doubles; the export therefore writes a picture-only and a sound-only asset per A/V file. adjust-transform position x is read as Pan * 100 / timeline height, so the export divides pan_px by the same image scale as the build. The sequence tcStart is ignored (the timeline starts at 00:00:00:00) and markers land on the first clip. With these, an imported handoff timeline matched the scripted build item for item.

A new timeline takes the project's size and input sizing. A 1080x1920 project set to scale to fit gave a vertical edit (previewed with scale to crop) letterboxed 16:9 clips while every item matched the EDL, so the build now sets useCustomSettings, the size and timelineInputResMismatchBehavior whenever either differs, and verify reads them back (settings_off). With that, a rendered 25 fps reel from 4K 50 and 100 fps S-Log clips matched the preview frame for frame at every cut, including 50 % slow motion and the J and L cut overlays.

Music ducking built as level pieces joined by Cross Fade 0 dB transitions (AddTransition on the audio items, centred) rendered within 0.02 dB (median) of the lab's ducked stem, 0.67 dB at most inside the ramps. A 4 channel LPCM clip appended with the other audio tracks locked played channel 1 at unity on both sides, within 0.05 dB of the preview (95 % of 40 ms windows).
Timeline.SetTrackEnable returns True on the Deliver page but changes nothing; it works on the Edit page. The skill does not use it.

FCPXML handoff, imported in the sandbox: the picture-only and sound-only assets gave exactly the EDL's tracks (V1 11 items and the dissolve, V2 the two J and L cut overlays, V3 the title as a Text item, A1 3 dialogue items at 0 dB, A2 the music at -8 dB with no ducking, A3 6 nat items at -12 dB, no doubled or stray camera sound). The timeline took the project's scale to fit; per-clip adjust-conform fill made plain clips fill the vertical frame, but a 50 % clip stayed letterboxed, so the export tells the user to set the timeline's input scaling.

Integration run (2026-09-30, sandbox, 21.1.0.14, a 30 s vertical ad built end to end: 38 clip pieces, 2 stills, 5 titles and 14 captions as Text+): the inputs of a Text+ shading element (2 outline, 3 shadow, 4 box) do not exist until the element is switched on (GetInput reads None and SetInput is dropped); switching it on gives the element its defaults (outline red, box blue at opacity 1), so the build sets every EnabledN before the element's colours (a Blue4 set first left the title box blue). A range of the graphics timeline reads GetLeftOffset equal to its start frame on that timeline (base 0). The Template tool of a Text+ on a timeline that is not current answers GetInput. Between two duck pieces of 2 or 3 frames Resolve squeezes a Cross Fade 0 dB so that it ends on the cut (asked 2 frames centred, got 1 frame before the cut) and the incoming piece's source start still moves back by its length; verify counts such a transition. VideoQuality is the bit rate in kb/s: 30000 rendered 23.3 Mb/s and 4000 rendered 3.2 Mb/s of H.264 at 1080x1920 and 540x960. The render's sound matched the preview mix (sample aligned, 50 ms loudness within 0.03 dB median, 0.4 dB at the 95th percentile, 3 dB at most in the last 0.3 s fade) and measured the same -17.6 LUFS; 60 Edit-page grabs and a 750 frame proof render matched the preview at median correlation 0.995 with no frame off. Resolve writes Edit-page grabs as uncompressed PNG (6.2 MB each at 1080x1920); verify stores them again compressed.

Fusion effects (2026-10-01, sandbox, 21.1.0.14, Builder A batches 1 to 3 on coded 50 fps clips and real footage proxies, 360x640 at 25 fps): a clip comp starts at the first frame its item is SEEN, frames under a transition included, on all three alignments (a 30-frame 50 fps item with a centred 8 at its head and a centred 6 at its tail: RenderEnd 72; a left-aligned transition at its head and a right-aligned one at its tail: 6 frames each; a right-aligned one at its head and a left-aligned one at its tail add nothing), and GlobalStart is minus the media frame shown at RenderStart (in point 40 with 4 head frames: -32). A still's and a Text+ comp run 1:1 (0 to n - 1); a 1.0 to 1.1 push on a still rendered 1.0, 1.05, 1.1. A retimed item (40 %, 25 frames) reports RenderEnd 9 for 9.6. Keys set with SetInput interpolate linearly: a punch keyed 1.0 at frame 5 and 1.25 at 10 rendered 1.0, 1.0, 1.1, 1.15, 1.25, 1.25 at 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 20; a TimeStretcher ramp showed every planned source frame (100, 300 and 50 %); a BrightnessContrast flash (Gain 1 - v, Brightness v) raised the level 0.51 to 0.90 and matched the lerp to white within 0.006; the ChannelBoolean RGB split keyed 12 px read 24 px between red and blue; a seeded shake table (Center through an XYPath, Angle, cover zoom 1.06) matched its affine model at correlation 0.97 with the fitted shift within 0.5 px, positive angles counter-clockwise, y_px down. A Transform Center offset is NOT scaled by Size (Size 2, Center + 0.1 moved 36 of 360 px). Speed Warp (RetimeProcess 3, MotionEstimation 5) gave a new frame every frame at 40 %, also with a keyed comp on the item. GetToolList lists the modifiers named after their tool and input (RE_MotionSize). Every catalogue transition placed at its length with place_transition; the rebuilt whip and zoom matched their previews at 0.997 to 1.0 per frame on real footage, and Motion Blur, Quality and Shutter Angle read back on Pan Left, Crash Zoom, Slide Left, Zoom In, Rotate and Camera Shake.

Animated Text+ (2026-10-01, sandbox, Builder A batch 5): 20 cues of 7 animations on a 30 fps 1080x1920 timeline built by the graphics snippet over two runs (a Text+ slot is 150 frames at 30 fps) rendered with every accent switch, word and character on the preview's frame and text_compare within its limits on all 20 (box 3 px, overlap 1.0, accent 2 px), also after verify had read every cue. A Follower colour or Size set as ONE constant value (one plain SetInput) drew no accent and no re-flow at all; the same value as two keys (first and last frame) renders, so every Text+ plan value is keyed. A still's marks count in PROJECT-rate frames: on a 30 fps timeline in a 25 fps project, marks 0 to 533 gave 640 frames (534 x 30 / 25, floored); the build never mixes the two rates (chunk 1 refuses a project whose rate differs from the edit's).

Effects integration (2026-10-01, sandbox, 21.1): three reels built end to end from cut lists (4 bumps on downbeats, a Fusion whip, a payoff push and a super_pop title on a 25 fps montage; 3 punches on voice-over words and 24 pop_highlight captions on an explainer; a punch, 5 animated titles, 14 captions, a left-aligned dip to black and, in a second build, a push on a still end card, a glitch and a light leak on a 30 s ad). Proof renders against the previews at the 36x64 pixel grid: keyed zooms 0.9958 to 0.9997 median per span, the whip 0.9995, the dip 0.9908 (the black frames are flat in both), every frame outside the spans 0.987 or more; against the same cut without effects the keyed spans fell to 0.66 to 0.92 at their peaks, so a missing effect would show. The glitch's bands and RGB split and the leak render (the leak raised the mean level by 22 of 255 in the render and 21.7 in the preview); their previews only approximate the shapes (the glitch preview draws the split, not the bands), so those spans stay unchecked. All 45 animated cues passed text_compare (worst box 8 px, overlap 0.97, accent 6 px, strength 0.199 against the 0.20 limit on one super_pop title). A whoosh's peak landed on the same sample in render and preview, 0.44 frames before its cut; the render's sound matched the mix (lag 0, level within 0.3 dB at the 95th percentile, 3 to 4 dB only in the last 0.3 s fade). Every call took 18.2 s or less.

Comp time at a rate that is not a whole multiple (2026-10-01, sandbox, fix pass 2): a 30 fps clip on a 25 fps timeline cut to 40 to 48 and 33 frames gave RenderEnd 46, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 54, 55, 56 and 38 for the exact 46.8, 48, 49.2, 50.4, 51.6, 52.8, 54, 55.2, 56.4 and 38.4: Resolve floors it, as for a retimed item, so the fx snippet accepts a span up to one frame under the exact value and keys at the exact rate (the 0.5 rule had refused 3 of the 10). Every punch read back and matched its preview (verify --grabs and --proof OK). A light leak centred on a cut keeps its visible half: keyed from item frame -10, it warmed the first frame of the shot by +27 of 255 in red and faded out over 9 frames. Glitch bands render (masked Transforms in the clip comp). A whip pair keyed as one eased travel with one key past the cut on each side (comp times before RenderStart and after RenderEnd are accepted) rendered with its sharpness falling steadily into the cut and rising out of it.

Stills under a transition (2026-10-01, sandbox, fix pass 2 integration): a still's comp keeps comp frame 0 on the item's first frame and runs from minus the head overlap: 6 frames of a PNG after a left-aligned 12-frame dip read RenderStart -12, RenderEnd 5 (GlobalStart -12, GlobalEnd 5); the same still with no transition read 0 to 37 for 38 frames, and a clip before the dip 0 to 84 for 43 frames of 50 fps. The fx snippet's comp time (RenderStart plus frames from the first frame seen) therefore maps item frame 0 to comp time 0 on a still too, so a push on an end card with a transition into it is keyed as planned.

Effects integration, fix pass 2 (2026-10-01, sandbox, 21.1): the three reels rebuilt from cut lists after the fix pass. Proof renders against the previews at the 36x64 grid, median per span: 4 bumps 0.9976 to 0.9992, a payoff push 0.9958, the Fusion whip 0.9995 (min 0.9985), 4 punches 0.9965 to 0.9983, a left-aligned dip 0.9908 (min 0.968); against the same cut without effects those spans fell to 0.66 to 0.92 at their peaks. A whip pair (clip comps, 8 frames up) scored a span median 0.976 (min 0.851, Resolve's blur is smoother than the preview's 8 samples) and its sharpness fell steadily into the cut and rose out of it (1.07, 1.02, 0.80, 0.50, 0.30 | 0.32, 0.53, 0.60, 0.63, 0.92, 1.50, 2.08), with no resting frame at the cut. 45 animated titles and captions passed text_compare (worst box 8 px, overlap 0.974, accent 6.1 px, strength 0.199 on a super_pop title). A synthetic whoosh and a hit landed on the same sample in render and preview, the hit 0.25 frames after its punch's word, the whoosh 0.46 frames before its cut; the sound matched the mix (lag 0, level within 0.3 dB at the 95th percentile, 3 to 4 dB only in the last 0.3 s fade). Every call took 22.1 s or less.

timeline_custom_rate.integer_rates: settable on an empty timeline (useCustomSettings 1, then timelineFrameRate)
timeline_custom_rate.ntsc_rates: refused through the API; the project rate must already be 23.976 or 29.97

multi_track_audio.pool_mapping_default: one mono track per channel of a wider stream (4 channel LPCM gives 4 mono tracks), a stereo track per 2 channel stream
multi_track_audio.append_with_other_audio_tracks_locked: one item on the target track: the clip's first audio track
multi_track_audio.plays: the first track of the pool mapping; a mono track plays at unity on both sides
multi_track_audio.item_channel_mapping_setter: returns True and reads back, but the render ignores it

fcpxml_import.markers: land on the first clip, not the timeline
fcpxml_import.input_sizing: the imported timeline takes the project's input scaling; adjust-conform fill is honoured on plain clips and ignored on retimed (timeMap) clips

new_timeline_settings.inherits: the project's resolution and input sizing
new_timeline_settings.build_sets_them: whenever the project's size or input sizing differs from the edit's

fusion_comp_render_end: (visible frames - 1) x media fps / timeline fps x speed, floored whenever that is not a whole number: on a retimed item, and on any media rate that is not a whole multiple of the timeline's (30 fps on 25: 46 for 46.8, 51 for 51.6, 52 for 52.8)
fusion_comp_global_start: minus the media frame shown at RenderStart

fusion_transition_comp.macro: one GroupOperator; published inputs take SetInput

transition_previews_real_footage.push: median 0.85 against 0.47 for a cut (close on real footage)
transition_previews_real_footage.slide: median 0.93 against 0.50 for a cut (close on real footage)
transition_previews_real_footage.brightness_flash_fx: levels at the flash differ: render 156, 214, 250, 252, 249, 172 against preview 167, 237, 255, 255, 210, 123 (6 frames)

smooth_cut_inside_one_take: clean on a 0.2 s jump inside one b-roll take (frame steps 2.4 to 3.0 against 2.3 to 2.5 of plain motion)
